blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic networking in the UK, at a senior level, is not about collecting contacts. It is about a small, deliberate set of relationships that compound over decades. The senior British executive who understands this spends less time at big events and more time protecting ten to twenty relationships that, together, shape almost everything that happens in their professional life.

The discipline is surprisingly simple and surprisingly hard. Track the relationships you care about. Contact them for no reason at all, at least twice a year. Remember a real detail from the last conversation, and pick it up at the start of the next one. Offer help before you ever ask for it. And when asked for help yourself, respond quickly and warmly, even if your answer is a careful no.

Having invested in this way for ten or twenty years, senior people find that their network is, in effect, a shadow organisation of its own — one that can provide introductions, quiet warnings, honest advice and, occasionally, a favour that would cost money anywhere else. It is, in British executive life, one of the quietest sources of real power.

items.q: According to the text, senior strategic networking in the UK is primarily about…
options: collecting as many contacts as possible
maintaining a large and constantly growing address book
attending the most prestigious industry events
a small, deliberate set of relationships that compound over decades
items.why: "a small, deliberate set of relationships that compound over decades" — o texto contrasta com colecionar contatos.

items.q: What does the text advise you to do when someone asks YOU for help?
options: Refer them to someone more senior
Delay your reply until you can help fully
Respond quickly and warmly, even if the answer is no
Always say yes, whatever the cost
items.why: "respond quickly and warmly, even if your answer is a careful no."

items.q: The phrase "a shadow organisation of its own" suggests that the network…
options: exists only on paper and never actually helps
functions like an informal institution that quietly delivers real advantages
operates secretly against the company's interests
items.why: Inferência: 'shadow organisation' = uma estrutura informal paralela que entrega introduções, avisos e favores — não algo sinistro nem inútil.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Giving help before asking for it strengthens a relationship.
Consistency over years is what makes a network powerful.
The busiest event-goer builds the most valuable network.
The size of your network matters less than its quality.
items.why: Inferência: o executivo sênior 'spends less time at big events' — o texto argumenta contra medir rede por presença em eventos.

items.q: Why does the author call this network "one of the quietest sources of real power"?
options: Because it is publicly celebrated in the press
Because it depends entirely on financial transactions
Because it works only for junior professionals
Because its influence is discreet, unadvertised and built over time
items.why: Inferência: 'quietest' remete à discrição — o poder vem de favores e avisos silenciosos acumulados ao longo de décadas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando uma sócia recém-nomeada. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Congratulations again — genuinely. Now, before the champagne wears off, let me give you the one thing nobody puts in the partnership handbook.

Having watched a lot of careers here, I can tell you the deals blur together after a while. What lasts is people. So I've pulled together fifteen names — that's your list. Not a hundred, not a Rolodex. Fifteen relationships that, over the next decade, will matter more than any single mandate you close this year.

Here's the discipline. Being introduced properly, by someone they trust, opens a door a cold email never will — so you'll spend your introductions carefully, and you'll always give one before you ask for one. Contact each of these people twice a year for no reason at all. Remember something real from the last conversation and pick it up in the next.

And a word of warning. Discretion is the whole currency here. If you become known as someone who repeats what she hears, this network quietly closes around you and you'll never feel the door shut. Guard that reputation as though your career depends on it — because, frankly, it does.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many names has Emily put on the list she gives the new partner?
items.why: "I've pulled together fifteen names — that's your list."

items.q: What does Emily say lasts, once the deals blur together?
items.why: "the deals blur together after a while. What lasts is people."

items.q: According to Emily, what does a proper introduction do that a cold email cannot?
options: It opens a door because it comes from someone they trust
It removes the need to stay in touch
It reaches a hundred contacts at once
items.why: "Being introduced properly, by someone they trust, opens a door a cold email never will."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says "this network quietly closes around you and you'll never feel the door shut"?
options: People will confront you about the leak directly
You will be excluded without ever being told why
You will be given a smaller list of contacts
The network will formally expel you in a meeting
items.why: Inferência: a exclusão é silenciosa e invisível — ninguém avisa; as portas simplesmente param de se abrir.

items.q: Which best captures Emily's overall message to the new partner?
options: Invest slowly and discreetly in a few trusted relationships, giving before you ask
Chase volume — the more contacts, the safer your career
Rely on cold outreach to build your reputation fast
Focus only on closing this year's biggest mandate
items.why: Inferência: ela reúne lista curta, discrição, dar antes de pedir e contato regular — o oposto de volume e cold outreach.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her approach to networking is entirely deliberate — nothing about that list is accidental." Deliberate here means…
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado, feito de propósito e com intenção clara — o oposto de acidental.

items.q: "These relationships compound over the years." To compound here means to…
options: grow in value cumulatively over time
items.why: To compound = compor-se, acumular valor progressivamente, como juros compostos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The best networkers ___ the relationships they care about, noting when they last spoke."
items.why: Track = acompanhar, monitorar — o texto pede: 'Track the relationships you care about.'

items.q: A quiet warning, in this networking context, is best described as…
options: a legal notice from a regulator
a discreet, private heads-up before something becomes a problem
a public reprimand at a meeting
items.why: Quiet warning = aviso discreto, dado em particular — um dos favores silenciosos que a rede oferece.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When someone asks for help, respond ___, even if you have to decline."
items.why: Warmly = cordialmente — o texto diz responder 'quickly and warmly, even if your answer is a careful no.'

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de networking sênior. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "She's happy to put in a good word for you with the chairman." To put in a good word means to…
options: say something favourable to help your reputation
items.why: Put in a good word = falar bem de alguém, recomendar informalmente para ajudar.

items.q: "I can reach out to a former colleague who now runs that fund." To reach out to someone means to…
options: make contact and get in touch with them
items.why: Reach out to = entrar em contato, procurar alguém — comum em networking.

items.q: "Good networkers always follow up after a first meeting." To follow up means to…
options: make further contact to maintain the connection
hand the contact to someone else
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, retomar o contato depois de um primeiro encontro.

items.q: "Don't cash in a relationship you've only just built." To cash in on something means to…
options: exploit it for advantage before it is ready
items.why: Cash in (on) = tirar proveito, 'sacar' o valor — aqui, cedo demais, antes de a relação amadurecer.

items.q: "A single introduction can open doors that years of cold calls never would." To open doors means to…
items.why: Open doors = abrir portas, criar oportunidades e acesso — o efeito de uma boa apresentação.
